questions: What is the exact definition of "p divides N an even number of times" - does this mean the exponent of p in N's prime factorization is even?
Is 36 included as a valid input value given that it's listed as the lower bound?
How should ties be broken when multiple 400 numbers exist at the same distance from A?
Are the prime factors of N required to be distinct from each other?
What is the precise mathematical definition of a "400 number" - is there a specific reason for this naming?
Should the output format include any specific spacing or formatting beyond one number per line?
Are there any additional constraints on the prime factors themselves beyond being distinct and having even exponents?
Does the problem guarantee that for every input A, there exists at least one 400 number ≤ A, or could there be edge cases where no such number exists?
answers: Yes. It means that for each prime factor p of N, the maximum integer k such that p^k divides N is even. In other words, all exponents in the prime factorization of N are even.

inline_prompts:
A positive integer N is a 400 number if and only if it satisfies both of the following two conditions:
- N has exactly 2 distinct prime factors.
- For each prime factor p of N, the maximum integer k such that p^k divides N is even. In other words, all exponents in the prime factorization of N are even. 
Process Q queries. Each query gives you an integer A, so find the largest 400 number not exceeding A. Under the constraints of this problem, a 400 number not exceeding A always exists.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
Q
\text{query}_1
\text{query}_2
\vdots
\text{query}_Q
Here, \text{query}_i is the i-th query, given in the following format:
A
Output
Print Q lines. The i-th line should contain the answer to the i-th query.
Constraints
- 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5
- For each query, 36 \leq A \leq 10^{12}.
- All input values are integers.
